title_original: AFM attendees face travel chaos after US flights grounded for hours
excerpt_original: Thousands of outbound flights impacted in largest “groundstop” since September 11, 2001.

blocks.text: AFM attendees face travel disruption this weekend after US authorities cancelled thousands of departing flights on Friday in the largest nationwide “groundstop” since September 11, 2001.

Airlines were allowed to resume schedules early on Friday evening after they were suspended for several hours when the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide moratorium due to “extraordinary circumstances and reasons of national safety”.

The US government declared the groundstop was due to a telecommunications outage impacting air traffic control centres, adding that it was not related to any threat, nor was there any connection to Thursday’s global Microsoft outage.

“Everybody’s safe,” US homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters. He stressed that the incident was not a repeat of 9/11. Flights scheduled to depart Europe for the US had been temporarily suspended.

At time of writing Screen had heard of market delegates who were either preparing to take off later on Friday evening, or were staying an extra night in Los Angeles and planning to head home on Saturday.

“It’s been quite chaotic,” said UK buyer of their itinerary as they prepared to depart on a rescheduled flight later on Friday evening. “Most of [our buyers] are flying on Saturday and hoping for the best,” one US sales agency executive said.
Travel disruption could also impact a packed weekend awards season schedule of screenings and receptions, culminating in Sunday night’s Governors Awards in Hollywood.
